title: scheduler: jittered slot reassignment and KV-warmup throttling
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Introduces jittered slot reassignment to reduce synchronized preemption, adds KV-warmup throttling to avoid cache stampedes, and exposes two new tuning knobs for batcher schedulers. Improves p95 latency under mixed workloads and prevents starvation observed in multi-tenant bursts.
description: Context: In high-concurrency mixed workloads we observed correlated slot reclamations and KV cache warmups causing transient starvation and p95 latency spikes. This PR implements two complementary runtime controls: (1) jittered slot reassignment to spread slot release/reassignment events across short randomized windows (configurable), and (2) a KV-warmup throttler that staggers cold-KV prefetches and enforces a soft admission budget per-slot to avoid simultaneous heavy prefetches. Changes: Implements a new scheduler helper (jitter_reassign) which inserts small randomized offsets before slot handoff and coordinates with the slot allocator to avoid churn; implements kv_warmup_throttle which tracks per-model warmup tokens and decays budgets based on successful cache hits; exposes scheduler.tuning.jitter_ms and kv.warmup.budget_rate config knobs; updates continuous_batcher admission path to consult warmup budget before immediate prefetch; adds lightweight metrics (jitter.delay_ms distribution, kv.warmup.throttle_rejections) and dashboard panels. Commits: "add jittered slot reassignment helper"; "implement kv warmup token bucket and decay"; "plumb knobs through config and expose metrics"; "perf tests and bench harness for mixed workloads". Changed files (high-level): runtime/scheduler/jitter_reassign.go; runtime/scheduler/slot_allocator.go (small API); runtime/kv/warmup_throttle.go; runtime/batcher/continuous_batcher.go (admission path); metrics/registry.go (new metrics); docs/benchmarks/jitter_warmup_readme.md; tests/perf/test_jittered_reassign.py; tests/unit/test_kv_warmup_throttle.go; ci/workflows/perf.yml. Motivation: Previous approaches (hard timeouts and global cooldowns) either caused head-of-line blocking or were too coarse-grained for multi-tenant bursts. The jittered reassignment spreads out reassignments to reduce synchronized pressure on the slot allocator and downstream kernel selection; warmup throttling prevents cache stampedes and reduces wasted kernel invocations. Performance: On internal perf harness using a 64-GPU cluster and mixed 75% short, 25% long requests we saw median latency change ~+2ms, p95 reduced ~18%, p99 reduced ~10%, and KV cache miss storms reduced by ~42% in burst scenarios. CPU/GPU utilization improved: fewer small kernel startups and more sustained larger kernels resulting in 6% lower cost/throughput token. Testing: unit tests for token decay and edge cases; perf tests covering staggered bursts, tenant fairness, and long-tail KV loads; load test in staging with warmup budget default of 10 tokens/sec. CI: initial perf run showed a flaky bench; reran perf pipeline with increased harness stabilization and all checks passed. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime.scheduler.jittered_reassign (default enabled for dedicated clusters, opt-in for hosted at 10% rollout), staged ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on regression signals (p95 increase >5% or error rates >0.1%). Backout: config toggle and immediate revert PR prepared if needed. Related: references ENG-4219 for prioritized scheduling work, ENG-4291 for KV cache prefetch follow-up. Checklist: design doc attached in Linear; unit tests added; perf benchmark included; docs updated.

review_comments: Ethan Clarke: Can you explain why a randomized jitter is better than exponentially backoffed retries for reassignment?

Priya Natarajan (reply): Jitter reduces synchronized events across slots; exponential backoff pushes responsibility to requesters and can still cause correlated retries across tenants. We benchmarked both and jitter had lower p95 in mixed bursts.
Maya Rios: Please add a test for the warmup token decay edge case where decay interval is extended by scheduler stall.
Priya Natarajan (reply): Added test_kv_warmup_throttle.go covering stall+decay scenario and updated comments to document expected behavior.
Liam Zhang: Suggest exposing metrics with rate-normalized panels to make alerting simpler.
Priya Natarajan (reply): Updated metrics/registry.go to publish per-minute normalized counters and added dashboard panels.
